title: A product of valuation rings has weak dimension at most one, and its fraction field product is a localization
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a set J, a valuation ring A_j with fraction field K_j for each j, and sets A = prod A_j and K = prod K_j, asserting that A has weak dimension at most 1 and that A -> K is a localization (source lines 30647-30654). The proof reduces flatness to finitely generated ideals: by the weak-dimension-one criterion it suffices to show that any finitely generated ideal I of A is flat (proof lines 30657-30659). It then exploits the product structure. Letting I_j be the image of I in A_j, the proof observes that I_j = I tensor_A A_j, so the natural map I -> prod I_j is surjective by the finitely generated tensor proposition, whence I = prod I_j (proof lines 30660-30664). Since each A_j is a valuation ring, each I_j is principal, say I_j = (f_j), so I is generated by f = (f_j) (proof lines 30665-30668). The substantive step identifies I with a principal ideal generated by an idempotent: taking e to be the idempotent with coordinate 0 or 1 in A_j according to whether f_j is zero, the proof writes f = g e with g a nonzerodivisor, namely with g_j = 1 where f_j = 0 and g_j = f_j otherwise (proof lines 30669-30672). Hence I is isomorphic to the ideal (e), which is flat because (e) is a direct summand of A, giving weak dimension at most 1 (proof lines 30673-30674). The final statement follows because K = S^{-1}A for S = prod (A_j minus {0}) (proof lines 30674-30675). The non-routine content is the idempotent factorisation that turns a principal ideal of the product into a direct summand.
